facts: The verb forms are often claimed to convey two kinds of information.
One kind of information is whether the event described in a sentence is present, past or future.
The information whether the event described in a sentence is present, past or future is deictic information.
A kind of information is whether the event described in a sentence is presented as completed, going on, just starting or being finished.
The information whether the event described in a sentence is presented as completed, going on, just starting or being finished is aspectual information.
It will be demonstrated in this paper that one has to add a third component to the analysis of verb form meanings.
The third component to the analysis of verb form meanings is whether or not the verb forms express habituality.
The framework of the analysis is model-theoretic semantics.
The event described in a sentence can be present.
The event described in a sentence can be past.
The event described in a sentence can be future.
The event described in a sentence can be presented as completed.
The event described in a sentence can be presented as going on.
The event described in a sentence can be presented as just starting.
The event described in a sentence can be presented as being finished.
